title: One battle away: Sri Lanka faces Singapore in fight for Asian Netball Final | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 14 August 2026 03:47
-     - 0

by Hishan Welmilla

Sri Lanka’s quest to regain the Asian netball crown reaches a crucial stage today when they meet arch-rivals Singapore in the semi-final of the 14th Asian Netball Championship, currently underway in Hong Kong.

The semi-final represents much more than another match for Sri Lanka. It is an opportunity to erase the disappointment of their earlier defeat to Singapore and move one step closer to reclaiming the Asian title.

During the group stage, Singapore defeated Sri Lanka 67-51, giving the defending champions a psychological advantage heading into today’s encounter. For the Sri Lankan players, that defeat could create an unwanted mental barrier. However, they must approach the semi-final as a completely new contest and demonstrate the confidence and determination required to reach the final.

Sri Lanka’s campaign has shown considerable improvement as the tournament progressed. They began with a 57-57 draw against hosts Hong Kong before losing to Singapore. However, the team responded strongly, defeating Malaysia and India before producing a commanding performance against Maldives to complete the group stage with renewed confidence.

Their improvement is particularly encouraging because the victories demonstrated different aspects of Sri Lanka’s game. Against Malaysia, they showed resilience and composure in a competitive encounter, while their 100-34 victory over India demonstrated their attacking strength. The 78-33 victory over Maldives further underlined their ability to maintain intensity throughout four quarters.

Singapore, however, will provide an entirely different challenge.

The Singaporeans have demonstrated excellent organisation, discipline and composure throughout the championship. Their biggest strength is their ability to control the tempo of a match. They are patient in possession, move the ball intelligently and rarely panic when opponents increase the pressure.

Their defensive structure will also be a major concern for Sri Lanka. Singapore are capable of putting pressure on the ball carrier while restricting passing options around the shooting circle. Sri Lanka’s attackers will therefore need to move continuously and create space rather than depending solely on individual brilliance.

The Sri Lankan defence will have an equally important role. Singapore’s attacking players are capable of converting opportunities efficiently, and allowing them repeated possession could prove costly. Sri Lanka must therefore fight for every rebound, intercept passes and force Singapore into difficult shooting positions.

The opening quarter could ultimately determine the psychological direction of the match. If Singapore establish an early advantage, memories of the group-stage defeat could return to the Sri Lankan players. But if Sri Lanka start aggressively and remain within touching distance throughout the opening period, the pressure could shift towards Singapore.

Sri Lanka must also improve their concentration during crucial periods. Against a team as disciplined as Singapore, a short lapse can quickly turn into a significant deficit. Accurate passing, controlled movement and intelligent decision-making will be essential.

Most importantly, the Sri Lankan players must believe that the earlier defeat does not define them.

They have already demonstrated their ability to recover from setbacks during this championship. Their three successive victories after the Singapore defeat have provided the confidence necessary for another battle against the defending champions.

Today’s semi-final is therefore likely to be decided as much by psychology as by technical ability.

Singapore have the advantage of having beaten Sri Lanka previously in the tournament, but Sri Lanka have the opportunity to learn from that defeat. They know where Singapore can hurt them, and they now have the chance to respond.

The winner will advance to the final, where either Malaysia or Hong Kong will await. That match will decide the queens of Asian netball.

For Sri Lanka, the message is clear: the past must be left behind. The players must step onto the court believing that they belong in the final.

One defeat should not define the champions. Today, Sri Lanka have 60 minutes to rewrite the story.

Harshitha Samarawickrama will be Athapaththu’s deputy.

In the last edition of the Asia Cup held in Dambulla in 2024, Sri Lanka beat India in the final by eight wickets.

title: St. Peter’s stamp their class at All Island U-18 Elite Rugby Sevens | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 14 August 2026 03:41
-     - 0

By Shamseer Jaleel

St. Peter’s College, Bambalapitiya, stamped their class by defeating Kingswood College 17/12 in the final of the Under-18 All-Island School Elite Rugby Sevens, worked off at the Royal Sports Complex recently.

The Peterites produced an outstanding campaign with attacking flair throughout the tournament. They remained unbeaten on their way to the title, underlining the strength of their junior rugby programme and the depth of talent emerging from the school. In the final, it was the Randles Hills school who led for most of the match, but the lads from Bambalapitiya staged a timely comeback to seal the game in their favour.

In the group stages, St. Peter’s recorded impressive victories over Lumbini College (24–5), Dharmaraja College (24–17), Maliyadeva College (33–7) and Ananda College (15–10), before completing their successful campaign with a 17–12 victory over Kingswood in the final. The side was led by skipper Hashara Madugasge, with Shirash Perera serving as vice-captain. The squad also included Adeesha Nadunajith, Janik Abeygoonawardana, Tharul Hansana, Sandika Niuwanhella, Thenuka Samarakoon, Geon Rajith, Rashwin Sabar, Kaweesha Kawushalya, Sajjad Shabeen, Fouzan Ali, Linuka Liyanage, Nethinu Anthony and Thoshitha De Costa.

The success further highlights St. Peter’s long-standing contribution to rugby in Sri Lanka. The Bambalapitiya school has consistently produced talented players who have gone on to represent club, national and age-group teams, while playing an important role in developing the sport at school level.

Their commitment to producing skilful and disciplined rugby players has made St. Peter’s one of the recognised rugby nurseries in the country. This latest Under-18 Sevens triumph is another indication that the school continues to invest in and nurture the next generation of Sri Lankan rugby talent.

The team was coached by head coach Rajeew Perera, assisted by forwards coach Amila Chathuranga and backs coach Randi Fernando.

title: Iga Swiatek will meet Elena Rybakina in the Canadian Open final | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 14 August 2026 03:40
-     - 1

Iga Swiatek will meet Elena Rybakina in the Canadian Open final after both players battled through their semi-finals in three sets.

Six-time Grand Slam champion Swiatek withstood an Elina Svitolina comeback attempt to seal a 6-3 1-6 6-3 win in Toronto and reach her first WTA final of the season.

The Pole, 25, has not reached a final since winning Cincinnati 12 months ago and had only reached one semi-final this year.

“It hasn’t been an easy season, probably the toughest one in my life,” said seventh seed Swiatek.

“This week has been really positive and inspirational for me, and it always kind of shows that you need to keep going no matter what.”

Later, Australian Open champion Rybakina sealed her place in the final, despite losing the opening set to Coco Gauff.

After winning four games in a row to clinch the second set, the world number two secured a 5-7 6-2 6-2 victory, having also come from behind to win her quarter-final against Naomi Osaka.

summary:

Royal Senior Team

DS Senior Team

Royal College Colombo will look to maintain its winning streak against emerging D.S. Senanayake College when the two schools contest their inaugural Water Polo Challenge Shield on Sunday, 16 August 2026, at the Royal College Union Swimming Pool.

The challenge trophy will mark not simply a new fixture, but the beginning of a new tradition in Sri Lankan schools’ water polo.

The event will bring together teams from the two schools across age groups from under-10 to under-20, with the aim of strengthening the sport at both Colombo schools and contributing to the growth of water polo in Sri Lanka.

For D.S. Senanayake College, the fixture represents another milestone in the development of a program that has steadily established itself in Sri Lankan schools’ water polo.

Water polo at the Borella school dates back several decades and has produced players such as Nalaka Senanayake, who went on to captain Sri Lanka in the 1980s.

The sport’s development at D.S. Senanayake College has gathered momentum since the early 2000s, with DS now emerging as a competitive force. Its young squad has demonstrated both skill and character, offering promise for the future of the sport nationally.

DS’ performance at the recently concluded Novices Water Polo Tournament provided further evidence of that progress, while the continued commitment of its players, coaches and supporters points to a program being developed for long-term success.

Led by Captain Dhakshina Perera and his deputy Thushane Koralevidanghe in the senior team, the DS squad has prepared diligently for the inaugural encounter, fielding teams from U10 to U20 age groups.

D.S. Senanayake College is coached by Seevali Gurusinghe, who brings considerable playing and coaching experience to the program.

His background in the sport, particularly in goalkeeping and defensive play, provides the current squad with technical expertise and an understanding of the discipline, positioning and decision-making required at the competitive level.

Royal College, meanwhile, will have a strong challenge on its hands as it seeks to protect its winning record on home turf.

Royal will also look to utilise its bench to test combinations and tactics ahead of the Royal-Nalanda encounter in a week’s time and the Royal-Thomian clash for the Hayman Trophy a few weeks later.

The ‘Spirit of Water Polo’ award will be a new feature of the fixture, placing emphasis on team play and discipline.

The award will be judged by the coaches of Royal College and D.S. Senanayake College, irrespective of the outcome of the matches. Teams from U10 through to U20 will be eligible for the award.

The organisers have also planned a carnival atmosphere, with a DJ and food stalls, while a papare band is expected to join the proceedings in the afternoon as the action heats up at Reid Avenue.

The fixture will mark the beginning of a new sporting rivalry and relationship between the two schools, with its continuation expected to provide further competitive opportunities for players and contribute to the development of Sri Lanka water polo. Match schedule is as follows:

1:15 p.m. – U14 match

2:15 p.m. – U10 match

3:15 p.m. – U12 match

4:00 p.m. – Diving Display

4:15 p.m. – U20 match

DS Senanayake Under-20 team: Methula Deelaka (Captain), Dhakshina Perera (Vice Captain), Vidusa Weerasekara, Sasen Silva, Senuka Lakdila, Wehan Aluthwala, Thushane Dilanka, Pramod Methsara, Dasis Sarathchandra, Yumeth Dissanayaka, Sihas Sarathchandra, Anuk Silva, Sandev Silva
